newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower on lack of bullish news.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower on lack of bullish news.

text.p: Taiwan share prices hovered in a consolidation on Friday and the index closed lower due to lack of major bullish news, brokers said.
The weighted index lost 36.07 points or 0.55 percent to end at 6,499.52. Turnover was an active T$51.18 billion.
Brokers said they expect the market to stay in a consolidation for next week as investors would likely remain on the sidelines ahead of the Mid-Autumn Festival on September 27.
"Without further bullish news, most people believe the index is unlikely to breach the 6,600-point resistance before the Mid Autumn Festival," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming.

Brokers noted that some corporate investors had begun an annual pre-holiday selloff to build liquidity ahead of next week's Mid-Autumn Festival, when many firms will reward employees and customers with expensive gifts.
"Individual investors also prefer to make their trading decision after the three-day-long weekend, in case something happens during the holiday," Hou said.

Profit-taking emerged in sectors boasting recent gains -- including electronics, textiles and plastics. Paper shares out performed the market, rising 0.38 percent. Taiwan Pulp and Paper gained 20 cents or 0.93 percent to T$21.7.
Asset-backed stocks drew minor bargain-hunting, with most active issue Pao Shiang up T$1.4 or 5.76 percent to T$25.7.

Acer Sertek Co, an affiliate of computer giant Acer Inc, saw its rally enter a third day after its Wednesday listing. As it did on Wednesday and Thursday, Acer Sertek surged by the daily seven percent limit, ending at T$42.8.
Slight improvement in economic indicators had failed to inspire overall buying interest, brokers said.
Taiwan's industrial output in August rose 0.09 percent from August 1995.
The island's foreign orders for Taiwan goods rose 0.03 percent in August from a year earlier to US$10.1 billion, the highest monthly high in 1996, the economics mininstry said on Friday.
